bugs: Progress counters are not idempotent. GenerateStatement::recordAttempt increments processed_accounts on every execution (app/Jobs/GenerateStatement.php:58, app/Models/StatementRun.php:36-43). An SQS redelivery or a retry after the increment counts the same account twice. My probe ran one job twice in a 2-account run: processed_accounts became 2, the run was marked Completed and the summary went out while the second account was still unprocessed.

DispatchStatementChunk increments dispatched_accounts before Queue::bulk (app/Jobs/DispatchStatementChunk.php:41-46). If the push fails part-way, the retry increments it again and pushes duplicates. total_accounts then ends up higher than the real number of accounts, so the run can stay 'running' forever, or the duplicates inflate the processed count.

ShouldBeUnique/UniqueFor on GenerateStatement does nothing because the jobs are pushed with Queue::bulk. Queue::bulk calls push() directly and skips PendingDispatch, which is where UniqueLock gets acquired (I checked this in vendor). So the duplicate protection the code seems to provide is not there.

Deterministic generator failures are retried 3 times with 30s and 120s backoff before they are counted. That is slow and wasteful for the expensive PDF step. A probe showed 3 generate calls for one bad account.
antipatterns: app/Jobs/GenerateStatement.php:27 – ShouldBeUnique with #[UniqueFor] is ceremony when the jobs are pushed via Queue::bulk
app/Models/StatementRun.php:11 – extra dispatched/processed counter columns plus a settleTotal dance, instead of an idempotent ledger or Bus::batch
app/Jobs/GenerateStatement.php:35 – queue set via onQueue in the constructor plus a QUEUE const, where #[Queue] would do
app/Jobs/DispatchStatementChunk.php:57 and GenerateStatement.php:71 – the summary-mail send is duplicated in two jobs instead of living in one place
app/Models/StatementRun.php:45-48 – the docblock narrates the method
strengths: Self-continuing chunked fan-out (1000 ids per chunk, using Queue::bulk) keeps each dispatcher job short at the 40k scale
Snapshots maxId so accounts created later are not included; jobs carry only the id, so deleted or deactivated accounts are still counted and the run finishes
The atomic conditional UPDATE on status=running ensures exactly one summary email
Slow work runs on a dedicated 'statements' queue with Tries, Backoff and Timeout attributes
Retries skip regenerating the PDF if it already exists
Strong Pest tests that drain a real database queue with queue:work, covering the failure path, no active accounts, deactivation mid-run and chunk splitting

bugs: DispatchStatementJobs dispatches all ~40,000 jobs one at a time inside a single job with #[Tries(1)] and no Timeout (app/Jobs/DispatchStatementJobs.php:11-33). On SQS, 40k sequential pushes will exceed the default 60s worker timeout and the SQS visibility timeout. The job is killed or redelivered, has no failed() handler, and total_accounts is never settled, so the run stays 'running' forever, or concurrent duplicate dispatchers send duplicate emails.

#[DeleteWhenMissingModels] on GenerateAccountStatement (app/Jobs/GenerateAccountStatement.php:24) silently drops the job if the BillingAccount is deleted after dispatch. No result row is recorded and completeIfFinished is never reached for it, so the run stays 'running' forever. My probe confirmed this: status running, 1 of 2 results recorded.

statement_run_accounts gets about 40k rows per run with no pruning (database/migrations/..._create_statement_runs_table.php:21), so the table grows without bound. The ledger's cascadeOnDelete on billing_account_id also erases counted results.
antipatterns: app/Jobs/DispatchStatementJobs.php:27-30 – a manual foreach with one dispatch per account instead of chunked Queue::bulk or Bus::batch
app/Models/StatementRun.php:44-52 – runs two COUNT(*) queries over the ledger after every single job (80k+ count queries per run)
app/Actions/StartStatementRun.php:16 – sets failed_accounts => 0 redundantly when the column already defaults to 0
app/Actions/StartStatementRun.php:20 – maxId is taken over all accounts rather than active ones (harmless, but inconsistent)
strengths: The idempotent per-account ledger with a unique (run, account) key and insertOrIgnore makes counts accurate under at-least-once SQS redelivery
Generator exceptions are caught inline and recorded as a failure right away, so the slow PDF step is not retried for deterministic failures; failed() covers mail and storage failures after retries
The atomic conditional UPDATE ensures one summary email
StatementReady attaches the stored PDF via Attachment::fromStorageDisk
Lean and readable, with fewer moving parts
Tests cover the failure path, empty run, duplicate execution and the failed() path; the suite is fast

v.rationale: Both suites pass (11 and 10 tests). Both use custom completion tracking (neither uses Bus::batch), an atomic status claim for a single summary email, and a dedicated statements queue. The probes showed different weaknesses. Impl-1 scales its fan-out correctly with self-chaining 1000-id chunks and bulk push, and it tolerates deleted or deactivated accounts. Its weak spot is non-idempotent increment counters: a redelivered job double-counts and can complete the run early (probe confirmed), and a failed chunk retry can inflate the total. Its ShouldBeUnique is bypassed by Queue::bulk. Impl-2 has the more robust idempotent ledger and handles failures better (no pointless generator retries). But its single dispatcher pushes 40k jobs one by one with Tries(1) and no timeout, which is very likely to fail or be redelivered on SQS at the stated production scale and leave the run stuck in 'running'. DeleteWhenMissingModels also strands the run when an account is deleted (probe confirmed). It is close, but impl-1 handles the stated 40k-account SQS scale and missing accounts better and has stronger end-to-end tests, so it ranks first despite its counter-idempotency bug.
